summary:
Space Mission Designer is an interactive educational game that allows players to experience the process of planning a lunar exploration mission. Players can choose their preferred rocket model, customize their spacecraft by selecting a platform, structure, solar panels, batteries, antennas, and scientific instruments by using the limited budget and make sure it does not exceed its weight capacity. At the same time, they must plan an orbit, manage limited resources, make mission decisions, simulate a lunar landing, and explore the Moon to investigate potential water ice.

The project addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by transforming complex space mission planning into an engaging, hands-on learning experience by using user-friendly interface. Instead of simply reading about spacecraft and lunar exploration, players can experiment with different configurations and understand how engineering decisions affect mission performance and scientific outcomes through this interactive game .

This project is important because it makes space exploration more accessible to beginners and encourages interest in STEM, engineering, and planetary science. By incorporating NASA mission information and scientific concepts, Space Mission Designer connects interactive gameplay with real-world space exploration.
details:
1.  What does it do or how does it work? 

The Space Mission Designer is an interactive educational game designed to introduce players to the challenges of planning a lunar exploration mission. It guides players through several stages of a space mission, allowing them to make decisions and experience how different engineering choices affect mission outcomes.

The game consists of five main stages:

Stage 1: Rocket Selection, Spacecraft Builder and Orbit Selection

Players begin by selecting a rocket model and spacecraft platform. They can then customize their spacecraft by choosing different structures, solar panels, batteries, antennas, and scientific instruments. Each component has different characteristics, such as mass, cost, and performance. Players must work within a limited budget and ensure that their spacecraft does not exceed its payload mass limit. They must also choose the orbit.

Stage 2: Resource Allocation

Players manage the spacecraft's available resources, including solar power, battery capacity, mass, and communication capabilities. They must allocate resources carefully to ensure that the spacecraft can support its mission objectives.

Stage 3: Launch and Lunar Landing

Players perform pre-launch checks, simulate the rocket launch, and make decisions during the journey to the Moon. They must also consider the landing site and landing strategy to achieve a successful lunar landing.

Stage 4: Explore and Collect Data

After landing, players explore selected lunar regions and use their chosen scientific instruments to investigate potential water ice. They can examine scientific information and simulated exploration results to understand how scientists search for water ice on the Moon.

Stage 5: Mission Summary

At the end of the game, players receive a mission summary showing their spacecraft configuration, resource usage, landing results, exploration findings, and overall mission performance.

2. What benefits does it have?

The game provides and interative way for players to learn about lunar exploration and space mission planning. It introduces fundamental concepts such as spacecraft engineering, payload limitations, power management, communication systems, orbital planning, and scientific exploration. The players can learn how the different spacecraft configurations affect the mission.

3. What is the intended impact of the project? 

Our goal of this game is to make space exploration more understandable and engaging for students, beginners, and people interested in space science.

The project aims to:

a. Improve understanding of the challenges involved in designing a space mission.

b.Introduce the scientific importance of investigating water ice on the Moon and its potential role in future lunar exploration.

c.Enhance problem-solving skills through resource management.

4.  What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? 

We used:

  • HTML: To structure the web application.
  • CSS: To customize the interface, layout, animations, and visual appearance.
  • JavaScript: To implement game logic, user interactions, and mission simulations.
  • React 18: To build interactive user interface components and manage application states.
  • Tailwind CSS: To create responsive layouts and style interface elements.
  • Three.js: To create interactive 3D visualizations of rockets, spacecraft, and lunar environments.
  • Babel Standalone: To compile JSX directly in the browser.
  • Visual Studio Code: For writing and editing the source code.
  • Git and GitHub: For version control and source code management

5. How is your project creative?

Our project combines rocket choosen, spacecraft customization, resource management, mission planning, and scientific exploration into one interactive learning experience.

A key creative feature is that players are not simply following a fixed mission. They make their own engineering decisions, such as selecting spacecraft components within budget and mass limitations. These choices influence the resources available and the possibilities for completing later mission stages.

6. What factors did your team consider?

We consider about:

a. Scientific Accuracy: We referred to NASA mission information and scientific concepts to keep the game connected to real lunar exploration.

b. Accessibility: The interface and gameplay were designed to be understandable for beginners without requiring prior knowledge of space engineering.

c. User Experience: Interactive interface and progressive mission stages make the players learn the lunar knowledge using engaging method rather than pasively reading information through article.
